quiz.question: When is a type annotation most useful?

answers.answer: When TypeScript already infers the correct type from a literal value
When the inferred type is ambiguous or incorrect, such as with JSON.parse
When you want your code to run faster at runtime
When you want to skip compilation entirely

quiz.explanation: Type annotations shine where inference falls short. For example, JSON.parse returns 'any', so an annotation lets you specify the actual expected type.

quiz.question: What is an additional benefit of explicit type annotations beyond catching errors?

answers.answer: They reduce the file size of your compiled JavaScript
They make your code self-documenting so others know the expected type without tracing logic
They allow you to use variables without declaring them first
They automatically convert values to the annotated type at runtime

quiz.explanation: Annotations serve as documentation: anyone reading the code immediately knows the expected type without having to trace through the surrounding logic.
